results.evidence: Ran `UV_OFFLINE=1 UV_NO_SYNC=1 uv run cottonwood --help` in the worktree. The output lists the subcommand `migrate   Create or upgrade the SQLite database by applying pending migrations.` The subcommand is registered in cottonwood/cli.py around line 58.

I ran `uv run cottonwood migrate --db <scratchpad>/ac2-fresh.db` on a path I had not created. It exited 0 and printed 'at version 1 (applied 1)'. I then opened the new file with sqlite3. `PRAGMA user_version` returned [(1,)] and `select * from sqlite_master` returned [], so there are no table rows at all. db/migrations/001_baseline.sql creates no tables. I did not read cottonwood/db.py or cli.py line by line, and I did not run tests/test_migrate.py.
results.quote: -- 001_baseline: the skeleton's starting version. Creates no tables.

results.evidence: test_second_migrate_applies_nothing in tests/test_migrate.py runs `main(["migrate","--db",path])` twice on the same file. It asserts the second call returns EXIT_OK, that _version(path)==1 afterward, and that the output says 'at version 1 (applied 0)'. db.migrate skips any migration whose number is <= the current user_version (cottonwood/db.py), so a rerun applies nothing. I ran the suite and all 13 tests passed. I did not read EXIT_OK in cottonwood/cli.py. I assumed it is 0, which fits the AC's 'exits 0'.

tests/test_migrate.py::test_migrations_apply_in_numeric_order builds a tmp migrations dir with 002_add_row.sql and 001_create.sql. 002 depends on the table 001 creates, so it only passes if they run in numeric order. It asserts applied numbers == [1, 2] and user_version == 2. test_migration_at_or_below_current_version_is_not_applied sets user_version=1 and pre-creates the table, so re-running 001 would fail. It asserts only [2] is applied and the version ends at 2. db.migrate (cottonwood/db.py:102-105) skips any migration with number <= start, and _apply sets user_version in the same transaction. All 13 tests in tests/test_migrate.py passed.

db.migrate raises FolderMissingError before sqlite3.connect when the parent is not a dir (db.py:94-96), so no file is created. test_missing_folder_exits_1_names_it_and_creates_nothing asserts exit code == EXIT_REFUSED (1), the folder path in stderr, and that neither the db file nor the folder exists. The test passed when I ran it (1 passed). I did not read the cli.py handler that turns FolderMissingError into exit 1 and the stderr message; the passing test covers that path.

results.evidence: default_db_path() returns $COTTONWOOD_DB when it is set and data/cottonwood.db otherwise (cottonwood/db.py:46-50). test_env_var_sets_the_database_path (tests/test_migrate.py:158) sets the env var, runs `migrate` without --db and checks that the env file is created. It also checks that no data/ directory appears. test_default_path_is_data_cottonwood_db (tests/test_migrate.py:174) deletes the env var, runs `migrate` and checks that data/cottonwood.db exists at user_version 1. All 13 tests pass. `git check-ignore -v data/cottonwood.db` matched .gitignore:19 `data/`.
